shared_elements: low-relief carving covering the front face of the slab
suggestion of a frontal standing human figure
circular disc motif (clear in B, possible in A)
justification: Both are tall, roughly rectangular blocks of weathered stone set upright on a plinth, with relief carving covering the principal face and, in each case, an apparently frontal human-like figure organised vertically from head to base. The difference is decisive in scale and legibility: B is a close, volumetric sculpture with a modelled head, arms and clearly incised disc and belt-like ornaments, while A is a distant, flat, largely effaced slab whose imagery cannot be read, so any correspondence remains generic.
